Can you cover for me on Friday? — Sure, as long as you give me a heads-up.
Could you take on the new client? — Yes, provided that I can drop the monthly report.
Can I leave early today? — No problem, unless the client calls.
Can I borrow your car? — As long as you bring it back by six, yes.
Vanessa, can I ask you a favor? Could you cover for me at the team meeting on Thursday?
Sure, as long as you send me your notes before Wednesday.
Of course. And could you also take on the presentation for the new client?
Hmm, I'm a bit spread too thin this week. I can do it, provided that it's not before Monday.
Monday is perfect. Thank you. I know this is extra work for you.
It's OK. But next time, can you give me a heads-up a bit earlier?
Absolutely. I'll tell you a week before, unless it's an emergency.
Deal. I don't usually take on two things in one week, but I'll make an exception.

Here is a small experiment. For one week, do not say a simple yes to any request. Add a condition instead. I can help, as long as we start after lunch. Yes, provided that you send me the details today. I will be there, unless my train is late. You will notice two things. First, almost nobody gets angry. People hear the yes first, and the condition feels fair. Second, your week becomes yours again. A condition is not a no. It is information. It tells the other person what you need to do a good job. And when you really can say yes without conditions, it feels like a gift.

Last year, my neighbor asked me to look after her dog for two weeks while she traveled. I love dogs, but I work from home and I have a lot of calls. So I said yes, as long as she could pay a dog walker for the mornings. She agreed. It worked perfectly. The dog was happy, my calls were quiet, and my neighbor was very grateful. This year she asked again, but for a whole month. I pushed back a little. I said, I can do two weeks, unless you find nobody else. In the end, we met halfway. Her sister took the dog for the first two weeks, and I took him for the last two.

First, I listen to the whole request. Then I check my week: am I already spread too thin? After that, I say yes, but with a condition: as long as it can wait until Monday. Next, if the other person pushes back, I try to meet them halfway. In the end, I ask for a heads-up next time.
